history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Jain (Digambar) shrine; keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. DUPLICATE FLAG: this row duplicates the already-written record 892.json ('jain-glass-temple-nagaur'), which documents the same Nagaur glass temple - that file was created under CSV row 892 'Jain Glass Temple, Tonk' whose town was corrected to Nagaur as no Tonk glass temple could be verified. CSV row 2152 'Jain Glass Temple, Nagaur' is a further duplicate of this same temple - dedup needed. The temple is a small Jain shrine in Nagaur's old city, famous for coloured glass/mirror mosaic work covering walls, ceilings, pillars, doors and windows, depicting scenes from Jain mythology and symbolising purity and clarity of the soul; it has a dome-shaped lotus-motif roof with a shikhara, glass chandeliers and a fountain tank, blending Rajput and Mughal styles (per 892.json - verify against 892.json's sources). Visitor reviews describe a small, clean, photography-prohibited shrine in bazaar lanes just outside the main entrance of Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh), managed by the local Jain community, with construction work ongoing nearby in 2013-14 (verify current status). IDENTITY WARNING: the exact location is inconsistently described - 'bazaar lanes outside the fort's main entrance' (Tripadvisor reviews) vs 'behind Kamla Tower, near Oswal Bhavan, Khas Bazar, General Ganj' (892.json) - and the presiding deity is unverified; coordinates here (geocoded to 'Shri Digamber Jain Adinath Mandir, Machhiyon Ka Chowk', not confirmed as the glass temple) are approximate - verify on the ground. The image in media/ is the first reliably located photo found; verify it depicts this temple.

name: Jain Glass Temple
town_description: Nagaur is a historic town in Rajasthan's Marwar region, dominated by the Ahhichatragarh (Nagaur) Fort. It has been a Jain centre for centuries: the Nagaur Chaitya Paripati mentions seven temples here, and an inscription records a Mahavira idol installed in Vikram Samvat 919; the ancient Sri Nagaur Teerth dedicated to Rishabh Dev (the 'Motamandir') is also in the town. The Glass Temple is a small, little-known Jain shrine in the old-city bazaar lanes near the fort's main entrance (its precise spot is inconsistently described across sources).

travel.railway: Nagaur Junction is the nearest station (verify distance to the temple).
travel.road: In the old-city bazaar lanes - one description says just outside the main entrance of Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh), another says behind Kamla Tower / near Oswal Bhavan, Khas Bazar, General Ganj (verify); ask locals for directions as it is easy to miss.
